{{Trail|Items}}{{#addtotrail:Alchemy|separator=' / '}} [[Category:Skyrim-Magic]] [[Category:Skyrim-Ingredients]]
This is an overview of ''[[Skyrim:Skyrim|Skyrim]]''{{'}}s '''[[Skyrim:Alchemy|alchemical]] ingredients''' (also called "alchemy reagents").

More information on each ingredient can be found on its individual page (see links in the [[#2|tables]] below). '''<span class="plainlinks">[https://gamemap.uesp.net/sr/ UESP's Skyrim Map]</span>''' and '''<span class="plainlinks">[https://gamemap.uesp.net/sr/?world=solstheim UESP's Dragonborn Map]</span>''' have the functionality to show the location of plants in Tamriel world space.

The [[Skyrim:Alchemy Effects|Alchemy Effects]] article lists ingredients indexed by magical effect and contains additional information about the relationships between ingredients, alchemy, and magical effects. A few ingredients are also classified as [[Skyrim:Food|food]].

Some ingredients (especially [[Skyrim:Salt Pile|Salt Piles]] and [[Skyrim:Garlic|Garlic]]) are also used for culinary purposes. Visit the [[Skyrim:Cooking|Cooking]] page for details.

With the [[Skyrim:Hearthfire|Hearthfire]] add-on, some ingredients (especially [[Skyrim:Salt Pile|Salt Piles]] and [[Skyrim:Chicken's Egg|Chicken Eggs]]) are also used for oven purposes. Visit the [[Skyrim:Baking|Baking]] page for details.

==Sources==
There are several ways to obtain ingredients:
* '''Purchasing from [[Skyrim:Merchants|merchants]]'''
** General merchants usually offer a few ingredients. Apothecary merchants offer many more, each stocking:
*** Up to 15 common ingredients
*** Up to 10 uncommon ingredients
*** Up to 5 rare ingredients
** Counterintuitively, your chances of finding a ''specific'' uncommon ingredient in an apothecary's stock are smaller than those for finding a rare ingredient. This is because there are so many more uncommon ingredients than rare ingredients, that: [(# of uncommon ingredients offered/total # of uncommon ingredients) < (# of rare ingredients offered/total number of rare ingredients)].
** Some ingredients can be bought and sold only if the [[Skyrim:Merchant (perk)|merchant]] perk has been unlocked on the [[Skyrim:Speech|Speech]] perk tree.
* '''Already-harvested samples'''
** You can find some ingredients on shelves or tables, in baskets, pots, etc., in various locations throughout Skyrim. They are typically plentiful in apothecaries' businesses and living quarters. Their owners may let you take the relatively inexpensive of these for free if you have done them [[Skyrim:Favors|favors]]. Mages and wizards around Skyrim, a concentration of which are [[Skyrim:College of Winterhold (faction)|people living at the College of Winterhold,]] tend to possess ingredients in their dwellings and rooms.
** Some types of NPCs and enemies may carry ingredients on their person.
** Ingredients can also be found in containers.
*** Certain [[Skyrim:Barrel|barrels]] contain multiple copies of a common ingredient.
*** [[Skyrim:Apothecary's Satchel|Apothecary's satchels]] always contain one or more randomly-selected ingredients (plus a 25% chance of containing a healing [[Skyrim:Potions|potion]]). These satchels are tagged internally in the game as of common-, uncommon-, or rare-type. Rare-type satchels always contain one common, one uncommon, and one rare ingredient.
* '''Harvesting from plants'''
** You can take ingredients from many of Skyrim's plants. Some of these are common and widespread, with thousands of plants growing in diverse areas, whereas others are quite rare and difficult to find. Once you have harvested a plant's ingredient, some or all of its flowers and stems disappear, allowing already-harvested plants to be easily identified. Harvested plants will later [[Skyrim:Respawn|respawn]], at which point you can again harvest their ingredients.
* '''Collecting from creatures'''
** Many [[Skyrim:Creatures|creatures']] body parts&mdash;meat, wings, heart, skin, horns, teeth, etc&mdash;are alchemy ingredients. When you kill the creature, you can collect the ingredient from its corpse.
* '''Catching passive creatures'''
** Various [[Skyrim:Passive Creatures|passive creatures]] can be caught to obtain ingredients, including bees, fish, dragonflies, torchbugs, and butterflies.
* '''Growing plants in [[Skyrim:Construction|the homesteads]]'''{{HF}}
** With [[Skyrim:Hearthfire|Hearthfire]] installed, areas of fertile soils can be added to the homesteads. These soils can be planted with a sample. The plant will grow into maturity after typically 2 days and there will be 2-5 samples of the ingredient on each plant (depending on the plant). The plant will not die and will respawn every few days after harvesting. However, not all plant ingredients can be planted. A list of plants that can be grown may be found [[Skyrim:Greenhouse#Food and Ingredients|here]].

==Standard Ingredients==
This table lists all of the standard ingredients in the game. You will experience a mild primary effect from eating an ingredient. [[Skyrim:Alchemy|Brewing]] two or more ingredients that share magical effects at an alchemy table will result in a potion or poison, with higher Alchemy skill levels resulting in stronger effects&mdash;longer duration, better fortifications or damage, etc. Special items such as Daedric Hearts and Void Salts are used in smithing [[Skyrim:Daedric|Daedric]] equipment and improving [[Skyrim:Nightingale Armor|Nightingale armor]], respectively.

Ingredients added by [[SR:Dawnguard|Dawnguard]], [[SR:Hearthfire|Hearthfire]] and [[SR:Dragonborn|Dragonborn]] are included in the table below, but a quick list of all the ingredients each add-on adds can be seen [[SR:Dawnguard Items#Alchemy|here (Dawnguard)]], [[SR:Dragonborn Items#Ingredients|here (Dragonborn)]] and [[SR:Hearthfire Items#Ingredients|here (Hearthfire)]]. For [[SR:Creation Club|Creation Club]] ingredients, see [[:Category:Skyrim-Creation Club-Ingredients|this category]].

There are 91 ingredients in the base game, with 5 added by [[SR:Dawnguard|Dawnguard]], 11 added by [[SR:Dragonborn|Dragonborn]], 2 added by [[SR:Hearthfire|Hearthfire]], and 1 added via the _ResourcePack.esl file, for a total of 110 ingredients. Additionally there are 5 [[SR:Unobtainable Items#Ingredients|unused]] ingredients, 3 of which were later used in Creation Club content and 1 of which is obtainable via a glitch.

Positive effects are highlighted in green, and negative ones are highlighted in red.

==Creation Club Ingredients==
A total of 73 ingredients are added by the following [[Skyrim:Creation Club|Creations]]:
* [[Skyrim:Bittercup|Bittercup]] (Ironwood Fruit)
* [[Skyrim:Fishing|Fishing]] (9 ingredients)
* [[Skyrim:Forgotten Seasons|Forgotten Seasons]] (Wild Grass Pod)
* [[Skyrim:Goblins|Goblins]] (Steel-Blue Entoloma)
* [[Skyrim:Rare Curios|Rare Curios]] (51 ingredients)
* [[Skyrim:Plague of the Dead|Plague of the Dead]] (Mort Flesh)
* [[Skyrim:Saints & Seducers|Saints & Seducers]] (6 ingredients)
* [[Skyrim:The Cause|The Cause]] (3 ingredients)
In addition, two [[#Quest Ingredients|quest ingredients]] are added by [[Skyrim:Spell Knight Armor|Spell Knight Armor]].

Positive effects are highlighted in green, and negative ones are highlighted in red.

==Notes==
*All ingredients which can be placed as world objects to harvest, or grown in fertile soil plots experience issues with scaling that can render them difficult, or impossible to actually harvest because of the default size not being used. Collision with other objects can similarly cause them to be unobtainable.
*If [[Skyrim:Survival Mode|Survival Mode]] is active, [[Skyrim:Fire Salts|Fire Salts]] are also used to create [[Skyrim:Food#Hot Soups|hot soups]].
*[[Skyrim:Taproot|Taproot]] and [[Skyrim:Dwarven Oil|Dwarven Oil]] are two of the few ingredients that share all 4 effects.
**You can also do this with [[Skyrim:Berit's Ashes|Berit's Ashes]] and [[Skyrim:Bone Meal|Bone Meal]].
**[[Skyrim:Human Heart|Human Hearts]], [[Skyrim:Corrupted Human Heart|Corrupted Human Hearts]], [[Skyrim:Simon Rodayne's Heart|Simon Rodayne's Heart]], and [[Skyrim:Mort Flesh|Mort Flesh]] all share the same effects as well.
**You can also do this with [[Skyrim:Void Salts|Void Salts]] and [[Skyrim:Fine-Cut Void Salts|Fine-Cut Void Salts]].
*Your Inventory says that [[Skyrim:Ash Creep Cluster|Ash Creep Clusters]]{{DB}}, [[Skyrim:Ash Hopper Jelly|Ash Hopper Jelly]]{{DB}}, [[Skyrim:Bleeding Crown|Bleeding Crowns]], [[Skyrim:Cyrodilic Spadetail|Cyrodilic Spadetails]], [[Skyrim:Dwarven Oil|Dwarven Oil]], [[Skyrim:Emperor Parasol Moss|Emperor Parasol Moss]]{{DB}}, [[Skyrim:Fire Salts|Fire Salts]], [[Skyrim:Frost Salts|Frost Salts]], [[Skyrim:Garlic|Garlic]], [[Skyrim:Giant Lichen|Giant Lichens]], [[Skyrim:Hagraven Claw|Hagraven Claws]], [[Skyrim:Hanging Moss|Hanging Moss]], [[Skyrim:Hawk Beak|Hawk Beaks]], [[Skyrim:Histcarp|Histcarps]], [[Skyrim:Human Flesh|Human Flesh]], [[Skyrim:Ice Wraith Teeth|Ice Wraith Teeth]], [[Skyrim:Mora Tapinella|Mora Talinella]], [[Skyrim:Mudcrab Chitin|Mudcrab Chitins]], [[Skyrim:Namira's Rot|Namira's Rot]], [[Skyrim:Poison Bloom|Poison Blooms]]{{DG}}, [[Skyrim:River Betty|River Bettys]], [[Skyrim:Scaly Pholiota|Scaly Pholiota]], [[Skyrim:Silverside Perch|Silverside Perches]], [[Skyrim:Swamp Fungal Pod|Swamp Fungal Pods]], and [[Skyrim:Void Salts|Void Salts]] all weigh 0.3 instead of 0.25. It is unknown if this is normal or a bug.
